techniques.why: sawtooth wave -- the canonical bright analogue waveform: every harmonic present, decaying 1/h; the raw material of brass-like, string-like and lead sounds
techniques.code:
kskew   = 0.02                              ; skew [0.02..0.5]: 0.5 a symmetric triangle, 0.02 a sawtooth
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.00245, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kdty0   poscil 0.0042, 0.057     ; age: shape/duty wobble on kpw
kpw0s0   = kskew + kdty0
aao0s0u0  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 4, kpw0s0, 0   ; wave seg0 imode4 copy 0
acln0   = aao0s0u0 * 1.000000    ; clean oscillator (pre-drive)
adrv0   = acln0                     ; drive 0: clean, no saturator stage
kagw0   oscili 0.0105, 0.7        ; age: amplitude wobble
asig    = adrv0 * (1 + kagw0)

skew.note: how far the symmetric triangle is skewed towards a sawtooth. One `vco2 imode 4` call does the whole travel and converges EXACTLY on `imode 0`'s saw spectrum at 0.02, which is measured in LCO_CONCEPT §5 and is why `triangle` and `saw` are the same body with different defaults rather than two instruments. Centroid 759 -> 2467 Hz and odd/even +39.9 -> +3.3 dB: a triangle has almost only odd harmonics, a saw has all of them, and the axis is the continuous path between. Comb contrast holds near 110 dB throughout -- both ends are exact waveforms, not filtered ones. Loudness 0.01 dB over the whole range.

leaning.gloss: just off symmetric, a little bite

techniques.why: square wave -- odd harmonics only, decaying 1/h: hollow and woody, the clarinet and stopped-organ-pipe family of colour
techniques.code:
kduty   = 0.5                               ; duty [0.05..0.5]: the ON fraction of the cycle
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.00245, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kdty0   poscil 0.0042, 0.057     ; age: shape/duty wobble on kpw
kpw0s0   = kduty + kdty0
aao0s0u0  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 2, kpw0s0, 0   ; wave seg0 imode2 copy 0
acln0   = aao0s0u0 * 0.578000    ; clean oscillator (pre-drive)
adrv0   = acln0                     ; drive 0: clean, no saturator stage
kagw0   oscili 0.0105, 0.7        ; age: amplitude wobble
asig    = adrv0 * (1 + kagw0)

duty.note: the ON fraction of the cycle, which is what duty means. This is the axis BJ's own example asks for — sharp at one duty, hollow at another — and it was impossible while the width was a structural constant. Its objective mark is the odd/even balance, not the centroid: at 0.5 the even harmonics are absent and odd/even reads +29.4 dB (that IS a square), and by 0.05 they are level with the odd ones at +0.8 dB. The centroid is deliberately NOT monotone with it (6304, 5398, 5262, 5148, 5373 Hz at 0.50, 0.35, 0.25, 0.15, 0.05) because a narrowing pulse first loses its top and then spreads energy back up. `vco2 imode 2` holds the level itself: 0.01 dB over the whole range, with no compensation applied.

fat.gloss: just off square, the evens creeping in

reedy.gloss: a quarter cycle -- reedy and forward

sharp.gloss: a spike -- bright, papery, almost a click

techniques.why: pulse-width modulation -- classic PWM: the duty cycle sweeps continuously from 80% down to 20% and back, ~2 s per round trip by default (1 s per half-cycle); slow/fast stretch or compress it to 4 s / 1 s, so the tone hollows out and fills back in
techniques.code:
krate   = 0.5                               ; rate [0.1..8]: how fast the duty sweeps, in Hz
klfo0    oscili 0.5, krate           ; -0.5..0.5, one half-cycle per 1/rate seconds
kpw0     = 0.5 + 0.6 * klfo0     ; duty 0.20..0.80, square at centre
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
apw0     vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 2, kpw0 ; imode 2 = pulse, kpw = width
asig    = apw0 - 0.6 * (2 * kpw0 - 1) ; remove the duty's DC offset, A*(2d-1)

rate.note: how fast the duty sweeps, in Hz. Restored: the parked emitter carried this axis and the harvest dropped it, so `pwm` shipped as a fixed 0.5 Hz sweep. Its signature is the BEAT and not the colour, and the beat comes back at exactly TWICE the rate -- 0.5 Hz reads 1.00, 1.0 reads 2.00, 8.0 reads 16.00 -- because the sweep is symmetric about the square, so the brightness peaks on both sides of every cycle. Depth is constant at 0.22 from 0.5 Hz up. Loudness 0.41 dB across the axis and 0.60 dB crossed with the register; the 0.1 Hz end reads 0.4 dB quieter only because less than half a cycle fits in a four-second render.

slow.gloss: a long breathing sweep, one pass a note

fast.gloss: a visible wobble, four brightness peaks a second

vibrato.gloss: at tremolo speed -- the duty as a texture

techniques.why: pure sine -- a single partial and no harmonic content at all: the reference tone, and the body of a whistle, a tuning fork or a sub-bass
techniques.code: asig    poscil 0.6, (kfreq * koct1)            ; pure tone

techniques.why: additive harmonic stack -- the general-purpose way to build any harmonic instrument colour: a seven-harmonic gbuzz stack doubled by a twin three cents above, so the pair beats slowly; knh sets how many partials, kmul how fast they fall away
techniques.code:
kad0    poscil 0.0004, 0.053         ; slow drift, upper stack
aa10    gbuzz 0.52, (kfreq * koct1), 7, 1, 0.68, giCos          ; harmonic stack
aa20    gbuzz 0.34, (kfreq * koct1) * (1.0018 + kad0), 7, 1, 0.64, giCos ; twin, +3 cents
asig    = aa10 + aa20

techniques.why: plain 2-operator FM (ratio 2, index 1.5) -- a carrier and one modulator, sidebands spreading as the index rises: the neutral FM starting point and the root of every DX-family timbre

index.note: the peak FM index: how many sidebands the tone carries -- how bright and rich it is. As it rises the spectrum brightens steeply while the loudness stays constant (a balance stage holds the level), so only the colour moves, never the volume.

mellow.gloss: few sidebands, close to a pure sine -- soft and round

bright.gloss: a full, singing brightness with rich sidebands

harsh.gloss: hard and edgy, the sidebands crowding the top

screaming.gloss: the brightest, most aggressive FM -- sidebands to the ceiling

ring.note: how long the bright attack rings before the tone darkens. Every FM note begins bright and loses its highs as it is held -- never its loudness. Low collapses to a dark body almost at once; high stays bright deep into the note.

quick.gloss: the brightness collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

medium.gloss: the bright attack settles into a darker sustain

long.gloss: stays bright well into the note before it darkens

detune.note: a second voice offset a fixed few Hz above the first, so the two drift against each other and the tone undulates. At 0 it stands perfectly still (the static escape); higher is a wider, more present movement. The offset is fixed in HERTZ, so it is the same at every pitch -- not a cent detune that scales with the note, and not pitch vibrato, which belongs to the synth.

pure.gloss: a single still tone, the two voices locked together

gentle.gloss: a slow gentle drift between the two voices

techniques.code:
kindex  = 0.200000                ; index [0..1]: how many sidebands -- how bright
kring   = 0.333333                ; ring [0..1]: how long the bright attack rings
kdetune = 0.600000                ; detune [0..1]: the doublet's offset, in Hz
ktm0    init 0
if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
  ktm0   = 0
endif
ktm0    = ktm0 + 1/kr           ; seconds since this strike
kbmx0   limit (sr * 0.45 / (kfreq * koct1) - 1) / 2 - 1, 0, 40 ; sideband room
kbtp0   min 4.0, kbmx0          ; brightest the band allows
kbnx0   = kbtp0 * (0.4500 + 0.5500 * (1 - min(ktm0 / 2.0, 1))) ; darkens as it rings
abl0    foscili 0.4, (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2, kbnx0, giSine ; the bell
abt0    foscili 0.26, (kfreq * koct1) + 2.0 * kdetune, 1, 2, kbnx0 * 0.94, giSine ; its doublet
abs0    = abl0 + abt0       ; the pair beats
abr0    poscil 0.46, (kfreq * koct1)        ; steady level reference
asig    balance abs0, abr0, 1 ; loudness held, beat kept

techniques.why: electric piano / rhodes / wurlitzer / dx piano: a struck tine or reed body with a metallic attack that fades back into it; ting = how much metal is in the strike, ring = how long it rings, hollowness = full body to hollow reed, strike = how hard the hammer hits

ting.note: the metallic 'ting' of the attack. this is the single feature that separates an electric piano from a plain fm tone; at 0 the instrument is only its wooden body. the ting fades back into the body as the note is held -- it loses its brightness, never its loudness.

none.gloss: no metal at all, just the woody body

soft.gloss: a faint chime on the attack

clangy.gloss: a hard bright metallic clang on every note

ring.note: how long the metallic part keeps ringing before it settles into the body. short is a quick struck-tine click, long is a sustained metallic buzz that stays through the note. both ends are taken from real electric pianos: the short end is a rhodes-like tine, the long end a wurlitzer-like reed.

short.gloss: a quick click, gone almost at once

long.gloss: a metallic buzz that stays through the note

hollowness.note: the body's character, from full to hollow. Low keeps every harmonic and sounds broad and piano-like; high keeps only the odd ones, which is what makes a reed sound hollow and nasal. 'tine' is where a classic electric piano sits. Its mark is the odd/even ratio and NOT the centroid, which is why both are reported: measured, odd over even goes +7.2 -> +77.4 dB across the axis while the centroid moves 53 Hz and the comb 1.0 dB. At the top the even harmonics are gone exactly, not merely quiet. Loudness 0.01 dB.

full.gloss: broad and full, every harmonic present

tine.gloss: the classic tine electric piano body

reed.gloss: hollow and nasal, a reed rather than a tine

strike.note: how hard the hammer hits: how bright the body STARTS before it softens. This shapes the tone, not the volume -- a hard strike is brighter, not louder (measured: 252 Hz of colour, 4.5 dB of comb, 0.06 dB of loudness), and the colour movement inside the note more than doubles along it. A soft strike still starts brighter than it settles, and that floor is not cosmetic: with it at zero, a soft strike on a body with no metal in it (`ting` 0) has no colour movement left at all and three corners of the cube FAIL the movement gate.

soft.gloss: mellow and round from the first moment

hard.gloss: struck hard, bright and biting before it settles

techniques.code:
kting   = 0.55                              ; ting [0..1]: how much metal in the strike
khollow = 0.75                              ; hollowness [0..1]: every harmonic, or odd only
kstrike = 0.64                              ; strike [0..1]: how bright the body STARTS
kbdx0   = 1.302 + (0.6 + 3.5906 * kstrike) * (1 - min(knote / 1.6, 1)) ; strike -> mellow, then holds
ktng0   = 0 + (1.5 + 1.0 * kting) * exp(-knote * 4.6594) ; the metal fades out of the tone
ktr0    limit 14.2, 1, sr * 0.45 / (kfreq * koct1) ; tine ratio, capped below Nyquist (see docstring: a cap, not a fix)
aevn0   foscili 0.12 * (1 - khollow), (kfreq * koct1), 1, 3, kbdx0, giSine ; body, even + odd harmonics
aodd0   foscili 0.30 - 0.12 * (1 - khollow), (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2, kbdx0, giSine ; body, odd harmonics only
atin0   foscili 0.30 * kting ^ 0.65, (kfreq * koct1), 1, ktr0, ktng0, giSine ; the inharmonic ting
asum0   = aevn0 + aodd0 + atin0
aref0   poscil 0.5, (kfreq * koct1)
asig    balance asum0, aref0, 10 ; colour travels, loudness holds

techniques.why: drum head / tom / timpani / taiko / conga / djembe: a stretched membrane resonating, whose partials are NOT a harmonic series -- that is what makes a drum a drum; pitched = indefinite tom to definite kettledrum, spot = struck in the centre or at the rim, tension = slack and dull to tight and bright, damping = ringing open or muffled to a thud

pitched.note: how definite the pitch is. an ideal stretched membrane rings at spacings that are not whole-number multiples, so it has no clear note -- that is a tom. loading the head with air in a kettle pulls those spacings towards whole numbers until a real pitch appears -- that is a timpani. this is the deepest thing about the instrument, not a tuning offset: the played pitch itself never changes here, only whether the drum sounds like it HAS one.

tom.gloss: no clear note, just a low woody thump

mixed.gloss: a note starts to emerge from the thump

timpani.gloss: a real singing pitch, a tuned kettledrum

strikepos.note: where the head is struck. dead centre wakes only the modes that breathe evenly across the whole skin, which is round and deep; nearer the rim wakes the ones that ripple around it, which is thinner, harder and more sharply coloured. a real player uses this constantly.

tension.note: how tightly the head is stretched, heard as which partials carry the sound rather than as pitch. slack leaves only the lowest ones and sounds dull and floppy; tight brings the upper ones up and sounds bright and taut.

damping.note: how freely the head is allowed to ring, as with a hand or a felt ring on the skin. open leaves narrow clear resonances that sing; muffled broadens them until the drum reads as a thud with a colour rather than a tone.

muffled.gloss: dead and thuddy, a cloth on the skin

techniques.why: gong / tam-tam / anvil / singing bowl / metallic percussion: true inharmonic metal partials (h 1.73/3.19/4.51) written as 2-operator FM at a 2.41 ratio

index.note: the peak FM index: how many sidebands the tone carries -- how bright and rich it is. As it rises the spectrum brightens steeply while the loudness stays constant (a balance stage holds the level), so only the colour moves, never the volume.

mellow.gloss: few sidebands, close to a pure sine -- soft and round

bright.gloss: a full, singing brightness with rich sidebands

harsh.gloss: hard and edgy, the sidebands crowding the top

screaming.gloss: the brightest, most aggressive FM -- sidebands to the ceiling

ring.note: how long the bright attack rings before the tone darkens. Every FM note begins bright and loses its highs as it is held -- never its loudness. Low collapses to a dark body almost at once; high stays bright deep into the note.

quick.gloss: the brightness collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

medium.gloss: the bright attack settles into a darker sustain

long.gloss: stays bright well into the note before it darkens

detune.note: a second voice offset a fixed few Hz above the first, so the two drift against each other and the tone undulates. At 0 it stands perfectly still (the static escape); higher is a wider, more present movement. The offset is fixed in HERTZ, so it is the same at every pitch -- not a cent detune that scales with the note, and not pitch vibrato, which belongs to the synth.

pure.gloss: a single still tone, the two voices locked together

gentle.gloss: a slow gentle drift between the two voices

kindex  = 0.533333                ; index [0..1]: how many sidebands -- how bright
kring   = 0.555556                ; ring [0..1]: how long the bright attack rings
kdetune = 0.650000                ; detune [0..1]: the doublet's offset, in Hz
ktm0    init 0
if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
  ktm0   = 0
endif
ktm0    = ktm0 + 1/kr           ; seconds since this strike
kbmx0   limit (sr * 0.45 / (kfreq * koct1) - 1) / 2.41 - 1, 0, 40 ; sideband room
kbtp0   min 9.0, kbmx0          ; brightest the band allows
kbnx0   = kbtp0 * (0.3333 + 0.6667 * (1 - min(ktm0 / 3.0, 1))) ; darkens as it rings
abl0    foscili 0.37, (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2.41, kbnx0, giSine ; the bell
abt0    foscili 0.24, (kfreq * koct1) + 2.0 * kdetune, 1, 2.41, kbnx0 * 0.94, giSine ; its doublet
abs0    = abl0 + abt0       ; the pair beats
abr0    poscil 0.44, (kfreq * koct1)        ; steady level reference
asig    balance abs0, abr0, 1 ; loudness held, beat kept

techniques.why: tuned struck metal bar -- glockenspiel / music box / celesta / kalimba: ideal free-free bar partials (h 2.76/5.4/8.93/13.34), brighter and thinner than a big bell, rung by a continuous noise exciter through a bank of high-Q resonators
techniques.code:
aexq0   rand 0.06, 0.5, 1          ; continuous exciter -> the metal is driven, a held note stands (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
k0qf0   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000, 20, 15000
k0qg0   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000 < 15000 ? 0.850 : 0)
a0q0   mode aexq0, k0qf0, 900      ; mode 1 @ x1.00, Q 900
k0qf1   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 2.7600, 20, 15000
k0qg1   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 2.7600 < 15000 ? 0.700 : 0)
a0q1   mode aexq0, k0qf1, 1025      ; mode 2 @ x2.76, Q 1025
k0qf2   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 5.4000, 20, 15000
k0qg2   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 5.4000 < 15000 ? 0.500 : 0)
a0q2   mode aexq0, k0qf2, 1150      ; mode 3 @ x5.40, Q 1150
k0qf3   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 8.9300, 20, 15000
k0qg3   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 8.9300 < 15000 ? 0.320 : 0)
a0q3   mode aexq0, k0qf3, 1275      ; mode 4 @ x8.93, Q 1275
k0qf4   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 13.3400, 20, 15000
k0qg4   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 13.3400 < 15000 ? 0.180 : 0)
a0q4   mode aexq0, k0qf4, 1400      ; mode 5 @ x13.34, Q 1400
amix    = (a0q0 * k0qg0 + a0q1 * k0qg1 + a0q2 * k0qg2 + a0q3 * k0qg3 + a0q4 * k0qg4) * 0.150
; The keyboard is not a volume control, and a `mode` bank on flat noise is one by
; default: measured, a single `mode` falls -2.91 dB/octave at Q 20 and -1.72 at
; Q 900, so a bank with mixed Qs has no one exponent that levels it and levelling
; at a single pitch left 5.2 dB of tilt over 110-880 Hz. `balance` needs no law.
; It is safe here because this body STANDS rather than decays -- on a real decay
; envelope a slow follower would flatten the decay itself. The reference holds
; this entry's own 220 Hz level, so nothing but the tilt changes.
aref    poscil 0.3986, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: ring modulation / AM at a 2:1 ratio -- carrier f times modulator 2f, so sum and difference land on f and 3f: a hollow ODD-harmonic tone (square-adjacent), with a drifting diode imbalance and carrier leak for the metallic edge

techniques.why: Chebyshev waveshaper -- a fixed transfer table (GEN13) holding odd Chebyshev terms up to the 11th, which map exactly onto odd harmonics: the controlled way to add drive, dirt and distortion colour

ash0    tablei adrv0, giCheb, 1, 0.5 ; Chebyshev transfer curve
asig    = ash0 * 0.55           ; level-match the family

techniques.why: pipe / drawbar organ -- hammond, tonewheel, church organ: three ranks at typical registration, an 8' principal, a 4' octave and a 5 1/3' quint, each its own gbuzz stack, each drifting at its own rate
techniques.code:
kregist = 0.5                               ; regist [0..1]: principal alone, or the full mix
kw80    poscil 0.00035, 0.061        ; rank 8' tuning wander
kw40    poscil 0.00045, 0.083        ; rank 4', incommensurate
kwq0    poscil 0.00030, 0.107        ; quint rank, incommensurate
; Drawing more stops on a real organ makes it LOUDER, and on this platform a
; parameter may not move the loudness. So the registration is power-preserving by
; construction: the upper ranks come up while the principal comes down, holding
; 0.46^2 + 0.24^2 + 0.16^2 constant. At 0.5 all three amplitudes are exactly the
; shipped ones. `max` under the root, because an out-of-range value would otherwise
; ask for the square root of a negative number.
kg40    = 0.24 * (0.30 + 1.40 * kregist)
kgq0    = 0.16 * (0.30 + 1.40 * kregist)
kg80    = sqrt(max(0.2948 - kg40 * kg40 - kgq0 * kgq0, 0.0025))
a80     gbuzz kg80, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kw80), 6, 1, 0.72, giCos ; 8' principal
a40     gbuzz kg40, (kfreq * koct1) * 2.0023 * (1 + kw40), 4, 1, 0.66, giCos ; 4' octave, +4 cents
aq0     gbuzz kgq0, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.4987 * (1 + kwq0), 3, 1, 0.60, giCos ; 5 1/3' quint, -1.5 cents
amix    = a80 + a40 + aq0
; `balance` and not a hand-computed normalisation, because this axis moves the
; SPECTRUM by moving a modulation index, and both `gbuzz` and `foscili` change their
; total energy when their index changes: unbalanced, the axis measured as a fader
; (3.5 dB on the reed, 1.6 on the flute, 3.6 on the brass, 1.4 on the organ) and the
; loudness also drifted WITHIN the note as the internal pressure cycle breathed. The
; reference amplitude is chosen to hold this entry's own shipped level to the
; hundredth of a dB, so the balance removes the travel and changes nothing else.
aref    poscil 0.2624, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

regist.note: the registration: the 8' principal alone, or the 4' octave and 5 1/3' quint drawn with it. Its mark is the COMB and not the centroid: 24.6 -> 10.7 dB, by far the widest comb axis in the wind family, because the upper ranks put energy exactly between the principal's own harmonics and nothing else in the library does that. Odd/even goes +2.8 -> -7.0 dB for the same reason -- the quint is not a harmonic of the 8'. Centroid only 620 -> 734 Hz. Drawing stops on a real organ makes it LOUDER and on this platform a parameter may not, so the rank amplitudes are redistributed power-preservingly before `balance` sees them, and the measured loudness is 0.02 dB.

principal.gloss: the 8' alone -- one rank, plain and hollow

mixture.gloss: everything drawn -- the quint singing over it

techniques.why: plucked or bowed string / guitar / harp / koto / pizzicato / violin / cello: ONE real string, set going and then left to ring -- NOT the ensemble string machine (that is `strings`, detuned saws) and NOT the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (that is `harpsichord`, gbuzz choirs). The string is a comb resonator tuned to the played pitch. It has to be fed the whole time so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking -- but the feed arrives as scattered, time-smeared touches and the ring is kept long, so what is heard is the string and not what is driving it. A continuous wall of noise into the same resonator is audibly an electric string driver: aggressive and restless. Its top dies away after the attack the way a real string loses its brilliance -- twice over, fast for the first instant and slowly for the whole ring. bow = plucked with a pick to drawn with a bow, pick = where the string is set going, from right at the bridge to at the middle, damp = left ringing to stopped under the hand

kbow    = 0.35                                 ; bow [0..1]: touches, or a steady draw
kpick   = 0.3                                  ; pick [0..1]: where along the string
kdamp   = 0.35                                 ; damp [0..1]: how freely it may ring
kstr    limit kfreq * koct1, 20, 12000
kfast   = exp(-knote * 20.00)                  ; the first instant's brilliance goes at once
kslow   = exp(-knote * (0.455 - 0.364 * kbow))                  ; and the string keeps losing its top all the while

kcut    limit (1050.0 * 0.42 ^ kbow) * (1 + (3.20 - 1.76 * kbow) * kfast) * (1 + (5.50 - 4.12 * kbow) * kslow) * (1 + kbrth), 60, 18000
aexd    dust 1.0, 300.0 * 13.0 ^ kbow                        ; the drive arrives as separate touches, not as
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.1100, 0.00710                ;   a wall of noise -- a wall is an electric
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0820, 0.00470                ;   string driver, not a played string. Each
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0640, 0.00310                ;   touch is then smeared out in time so none

aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0260, 0.00079                ;   buries the instrument's own colour

bow.note: how the string is set going, and that is the whole difference between a guitar and a cello. A pick or a fingernail lets go in an instant, so everything in the string is woken at once and the sound arrives bright and then falls away. A bow never lets go: the hair grabs and slips and grabs again, feeding the string the whole time, so the top is rubbed off but nothing dies -- the tone stands and breathes instead. In the code this is how DENSELY the drive arrives: separate touches at the plucked end, a steady draw at the bowed one. Measured across the axis the colour travels from 4812 Hz down to 3463 Hz while how sharply the string rings does not change (32.9 -> 34.1 dB) and the loudness moves 0.05 dB.

plucked.gloss: picked and let go: bright at the front, then darkening

bowed.gloss: drawn with a bow: standing, breathing, the top rubbed off

pick.note: where along its length the string is set going. This is not a tone control, it is geometry: a string cannot be given any energy at a harmonic whose still point falls exactly where you touch it, so that harmonic is simply missing. Right by the bridge the touch is at a twentieth of the length and only the very high ones are lost, so the sound is thin, hard and nasal; at the middle every even harmonic goes at once and the sound is hollow and woody, a clarinet made of string. Measured at the middle, harmonics 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 sit 37 to 43 dB below the fundamental -- 30 to 45 dB lower than the same harmonics played at the bridge -- which is the real thing and not an effect. It moves 333 Hz of colour and 0.00 dB of loudness.

bridge.gloss: played hard by the bridge: thin, wiry, nasal

middle.gloss: over the middle: hollow and woody, the even harmonics gone

damp.note: how freely the string is allowed to ring, as with the flat of the hand laid on it. Open, the resonances are narrow and the string sings a clear note; stopped, they broaden and the string reads as a knock with a colour rather than a pitch. It never stops ringing altogether -- a string whose resonance is let go stops sounding like a string at all and starts sounding like the thing driving it. Measured as how far the sound BETWEEN the harmonics sits below the harmonics themselves: 37.6 dB open, 29.7 dB stopped. The colour follows it a little (3972 -> 4314 Hz) because a broad resonance passes more of the drive's own top, and the loudness moves 0.02 dB.

open.gloss: left to ring, a clear singing note

damped.gloss: a hand resting on it, controlled

muted.gloss: palm-muted: a knock with a colour, barely a pitch

techniques.why: supersaw / hypersaw -- the trance and rave lead: a stack of seven saws detuned a few cents apart, and the beating between them IS the sound
mandatory_flags: detune/unison is a voice-level effect, not a cycle property
techniques.code:

kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0

asu0x1  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0035 * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x2  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.9965 * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x3  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0071 * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x4  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.9929 * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x5  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0110 * (1 + kvdr0), 0

techniques.why: hard sync / oscillator sync -- the classic tearing sync lead: a slave saw restarted by the master every cycle, its ratio sweeping 1.5x..3.7x
mandatory_flags: true hard sync is not yet a supported kind; approximated with FM
techniques.code:
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kswp0   oscili 1.1, 0.16            ; slave-ratio sweep
krat0   = 2.6 + kswp0            ; 1.5 .. 3.7 x master
azro0   = 0

techniques.why: harpsichord / cembalo / spinet / virginal -- a plucked keyboard: two bright gbuzz choirs, an 8' and a 4' a hair sharp, drifting against each other; the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (a real plucked string is `string`)

ah40    gbuzz 0.24, (kfreq * koct1) * 2.0031 * (1 + khw40), 6, 1, 0.72, giCos ; 4' choir

techniques.why: chiptune -- the NES / Game Boy / C64 voice: the duty cycle STEPS between three fixed settings (12.5%, 25%, 50%) instead of gliding, giving the hard retro timbre switches
techniques.code:

kdt0    = (kst0 > 0.5 ? 0.125 : (kst0 > -0.5 ? 0.25 : 0.5))
kdw0    tonek kdt0, 30          ; de-click the duty step
ach0    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1), 2, kdw0     ; stepped chip duty
asig    = ach0 - 0.6 * (2 * kdw0 - 1) ; remove the duty's DC offset, A*(2d-1)

techniques.why: theremin / ondes martenot / musical saw -- the breathing, near-vocal purity of a swept heterodyne tone: an almost pure tone whose odd harmonics waver slowly under a heterodyne nonlinearity
mandatory_flags: theremin's character is continuous pitch/amplitude glide, not a fixed spectrum; approximated as a pure tone
techniques.code:

kndx0   = 0.42 + 0.34 * kwv0       ; heterodyne mix depth
asig    foscili 0.55, (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2, kndx0, giSine ; heterodyne nonlinearity

techniques.why: sub bass -- the 808-style low pair: a pure fundamental with a divider octave beneath it
mandatory_flags: 'sub' is a register/mix role, not a distinct spectrum; approximated as a pure sine
techniques.code:

asb0    gbuzz 0.28, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.5 * (1 + ksbw0), 2, 1, 0.55, giCos ; sub octave (divider)

techniques.why: analogue oscillator / vco / minimoog / juno / prophet / analogue synth: wave morphs continuously triangle to saw to square to pulse; drive is the mixer pushed past unity into a soft limiter (careful: it makes a saw ROUNDER and darker, only a triangle brighter); fat = detuned unison, age = analogue instability

drive.note: counter-intuitive, and this is the real behaviour of the hardware this models: on a saw or a narrow pulse, drive makes the tone ROUNDER and DARKER (the soft limiter rounds off the sharp edge and takes highs away); on a triangle, drive ADDS harmonics and makes it BRIGHTER. Never describe drive as simply 'brighter'.

worn.gloss: gentle analogue life -- pitch, level and shape all drifting slightly

old.gloss: unstable, wandering pitch and level, worn-in gear

techniques.why: struck glass / a glass pad -- a bright inharmonic sheen: six `mode` resonators at glass ratios (1, 2.71, 3.83, 5.17, 6.61, 8.09) at very high Q (1400-2000) under a continuous noise exciter, so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking. Not a harmonic series: that is the substance of glass, not a detail. Measured on this build: the spectrum follows the keyboard exactly, and like every noise-driven `mode` bank it gets about 1.8 dB quieter per octave upward, because a noise-driven resonator emits power ~ Q/f.
techniques.code:
aexq0   rand 0.05, 0.5, 1          ; continuous exciter -> the metal is driven, a held note stands (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
k0qf0   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000, 20, 15000
k0qg0   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000 < 15000 ? 1.000 : 0)
a0q0   mode aexq0, k0qf0, 1400      ; mode 1 @ x1.00, Q 1400
k0qf1   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 2.7100, 20, 15000
k0qg1   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 2.7100 < 15000 ? 0.620 : 0)
a0q1   mode aexq0, k0qf1, 1520      ; mode 2 @ x2.71, Q 1520
k0qf2   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 3.8300, 20, 15000
k0qg2   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 3.8300 < 15000 ? 0.440 : 0)
a0q2   mode aexq0, k0qf2, 1640      ; mode 3 @ x3.83, Q 1640
k0qf3   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 5.1700, 20, 15000
k0qg3   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 5.1700 < 15000 ? 0.300 : 0)
a0q3   mode aexq0, k0qf3, 1760      ; mode 4 @ x5.17, Q 1760
k0qf4   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 6.6100, 20, 15000
k0qg4   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 6.6100 < 15000 ? 0.200 : 0)
a0q4   mode aexq0, k0qf4, 1880      ; mode 5 @ x6.61, Q 1880
k0qf5   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 8.0900, 20, 15000
k0qg5   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 8.0900 < 15000 ? 0.130 : 0)
a0q5   mode aexq0, k0qf5, 2000      ; mode 6 @ x8.09, Q 2000
amix    = (a0q0 * k0qg0 + a0q1 * k0qg1 + a0q2 * k0qg2 + a0q3 * k0qg3 + a0q4 * k0qg4 + a0q5 * k0qg5) * 0.150
; The keyboard is not a volume control, and a `mode` bank on flat noise is one by
; default: measured, a single `mode` falls -2.91 dB/octave at Q 20 and -1.72 at
; Q 900, so a bank with mixed Qs has no one exponent that levels it and levelling
; at a single pitch left 5.6 dB of tilt over 110-880 Hz. `balance` needs no law.
; It is safe here because this body STANDS rather than decays -- on a real decay
; envelope a slow follower would flatten the decay itself. The reference holds
; this entry's own 220 Hz level, so nothing but the tilt changes.
aref    poscil 0.4472, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: white noise -- `rand`, a flat full-spectrum hiss with no pitch at all. The keyboard does NOT change it (measured: identical at 110 and 880 Hz); it is a bed, and pitch has to come from whatever it is filtered or ring-modulated with. The raw material every other bed here is built from.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
asig    = anz0 * 0.6                ; white noise (flat hiss)

techniques.why: pink noise -- `pinkish`, a 1/f tilt over `rand`: the same hiss with the top taken off, softer and warmer, and much closer to the spectrum of real environmental sound than white noise is. No pitch; the keyboard does not change it.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
asig    pinkish anz0               ; pink noise (1/f tilt)

techniques.why: wind / breeze / gust -- a wide `reson` band walking up and down over noise, driven by two incommensurate slow oscillators (0.071 and 0.113 Hz) so the gusts never fall into a pattern: the band rises from 380 to about 1420 Hz as it blows AND gets louder at the same time, which is what makes it read as air moving rather than as a filter sweep. No pitch, and the keyboard does not change it.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
kgsa0   poscil 0.5, 0.071            ; gust, slow
kgsb0   poscil 0.3, 0.113            ; second, incommensurate
kgst0   = 0.5 + kgsa0 + kgsb0  ; gust strength
awd0    reson anz0, 380 + 520 * kgst0, 400, 2 ; higher when it blows
asig    = awd0 * (0.30 + 0.42 * kgst0) ; and louder

techniques.why: rain / rainfall / drizzle -- a real particle bed, not a hiss: `dust2` fires about 1400 separate impacts a second and each one rings a surface (`reson` at 2400 Hz), over a darker wash of merged distant drops, with the whole shower swelling and easing at 0.043 Hz. This is the architecture for anything made of many small events -- change the rate and what it is made of changes with it. No pitch, and the keyboard does not change it.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
adrp0   dust2 0.5, 1400              ; the patter: ~1400 impacts/s
arzn0   reson adrp0, 2400, 1800, 2 ; each drop rings the surface
awsh0   atone anz0, 2000             ; distant drops, merged to a wash
kint0   poscil 0.22, 0.043           ; the rain comes and goes
asig    = (arzn0 * 0.94 + awsh0 * 0.51) * (1 + kint0)

techniques.why: surf / ocean / the sea -- two bands of noise moved by one swell: a low body (`tone` 700) that is always there and a bright break (`atone` 1800) that only arrives at the top of the swell, and arrives as the SQUARE of it, so the crest breaks instead of fading in. Two incommensurate swells (0.055 and 0.083 Hz, ~18 s and ~12 s) keep the sea from repeating. No pitch; the keyboard does not change it.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
kswa0   poscil 0.5, 0.055            ; swell, ~18 s
kswb0   poscil 0.22, 0.083           ; second, incommensurate
kswl0   = 0.5 + kswa0 + kswb0  ; 0 .. 1.2
asfl0   tone anz0, 700               ; the body of the wave
asfb0   atone anz0, 1800             ; the break, bright
asig    = asfl0 * (0.35 + 0.35 * kswl0) + asfb0 * 0.30 * kswl0 * kswl0

techniques.why: thunder / a distant storm / rumble -- low broadband body (`tone` 400) rolled by three incommensurate slow oscillators (0.037, 0.061, 0.091 Hz) so the rumble keeps folding over itself and never pulses. No pitch, and the keyboard does not change it.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
krla0   poscil 0.5, 0.037            ; the roll
krlb0   poscil 0.28, 0.061
krlc0   poscil 0.16, 0.091
athl0   tone anz0, 400               ; low broadband body
asig    = athl0 * (0.80 + 0.61 * (krla0 + krlb0 + krlc0))

techniques.why: hiss / static / tape hiss -- `atone` at 6000 Hz over noise: only the top left, the sound of a dead channel. No pitch; the keyboard does not change it.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
asig    atone anz0, 6000            ; hiss/static: bright high noise
asig    = asig * 0.7

techniques.why: crackle / fire / a campfire -- the same particle architecture as `rain` at a hundredth of the rate: `dust2` fires about 22 pops a second and each rings wood (`reson` 1600 Hz, wide), over a fine sizzle that breathes at 0.13 Hz. Sparse enough that individual events are heard, which is the difference between fire and rain. No pitch, and the keyboard does not change it.
techniques.code:
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
acrk0   dust2 0.8, 22                ; ~22 pops a second
apop0   reson acrk0, 1600, 1200, 2 ; each pop rings the wood
kbed0   poscil 0.5, 0.13             ; the fire breathes

techniques.why: a sung human voice on an open 'ahh' -- real formant synthesis, not an additive sketch: a `vco2` glottal source tilted by `tone`, through three `reson` formants at 600 / 1040 / 2250 Hz, with three-rate period jitter and two-rate amplitude shimmer so it is never a steady tone. The pitch follows the keyboard and the formants do NOT, which is what makes it a voice -- and also its ceiling: measured on this build it is level within 3.3 dB from 110 to 660 Hz and then falls 13.8 dB at 880, because above the first formant no harmonic can land in it any more. Usable up to roughly its own F1.

techniques.why: a real Rhodes tine piano that RINGS AND FADES BY ITSELF -- Csound's own `fmrhode` model, re-struck on each note through `changed2(ktrig)`/`reinit`: a bell-like metallic attack over a woody body, and the note dies whether or not the key is held. Measured on this build: half-life 566-599 ms and peak flat at 0.57 from 110 to 1760 Hz. For the version that STANDS as long as the key is held -- the spectrum source, with the synth's envelope doing the striking -- use `fm_ep` instead; that is the same instrument as a standing tone.
techniques.code:
; --- osc 0: rhodes -- struck instrument, decays on its own ---
  if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
    reinit strike0
  endif
strike0:
  asig    fmrhode 0.7821, (kfreq * koct1), 1, 1, 0.01, 6, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1
  rireturn

techniques.why: a real Wurlitzer reed piano that RINGS AND FADES BY ITSELF -- Csound's own `fmwurlie`, re-struck per note: reedier and barkier than a Rhodes, its brightness sitting ON the odd harmonics rather than off the comb, and it rings longer. Measured: half-life 676-718 ms, peak flat at 0.55 across the register. `fm_ep` is the standing-tone counterpart.

techniques.why: a real struck aluminium bar that RINGS AND FADES BY ITSELF -- Csound's `vibes` model, re-struck per note: a soft mallet, sweet and round rather than clangorous, and short. Measured: half-life 284-315 ms. The model's own 15 dB register tilt is undone in the code by a 0.73 exponent below 440 Hz, so peak runs 0.42 to 0.62 across the register instead of 3.5 to 0.6. Two structural limits of the model, both measured and neither tunable: it collapses about 10 dB above ~4 kHz, and its pitch freezes at the strike, so a glide is not followed within a note. `struck_bar` is the standing-tone mallet counterpart.
techniques.code:
; --- osc 0: vibraphone -- struck instrument, decays on its own ---
  if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
    reinit strike0
  endif
strike0:
  kvtl0   limit (kfreq * koct1) / 440, 0.001, 1   ; 1.0 at and above 440 Hz
  kvamp0  = 0.1863 * kvtl0 ^ 0.73   ; undo the model's 15 dB register tilt
  asig    vibes kvamp0, (kfreq * koct1), 0.9, 0.5, 4, 6, 0.01, 1, 0.5
  rireturn

techniques.why: accordion / harmonium / bandoneon / melodica -- a FREE reed: a tongue of metal beating in a slot, driven by bellows. Three `gbuzz` stacks, one at pitch and two spread +21 and -16 cents, so the reeds BEAT against each other -- that beat is what a musette is, and it is measured, not decorative: depth 0.04 with one reed and 0.28 with three, at 2.3 Hz. The bellows are the instrument's gesture and never hold still, so a slow lean at 0.19 Hz opens the harmonic series and pulls the reed slightly sharp together; that lean, not the beat, is what keeps a single-reed setting moving. `gbuzz` normalises to PEAK, so the closed-form `knrm` holds one loudness while the harmonic count travels: measured 0.07 dB across the whole parameter cube and 0.4 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz. Reedier and buzzier than `clarinet`, which is a cylindrical BEATING reed with only odd harmonics; this one keeps the full series (odd/even balance +5.1 dB).

musette.note: one reed or three. Above 0 two more reeds sound +21 and -16 cents away and the three BEAT: measured depth 0.01 -> 0.29 at 2.3 Hz. This is an amplitude beat, so it is deliberately almost invisible to the colour meters (centroid moves 1796 -> 1434 Hz as the beat fills in); `lco_measure.beat` is what reads it.

single.gloss: one reed, dead straight -- a harmonium, no beat at all

slight.gloss: a second reed just audible, the tone starting to shimmer

wet.gloss: three reeds full up -- the widest, most seasick tuning

press.note: how hard the bellows lean on the reed, as harmonic richness. It deepens the harmonic comb (44.1 -> 49.1 dB) rather than simply brightening: measured centroid 1513 -> 1702 Hz, loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

soft.gloss: barely leaning -- a thin, sweet, almost flute-like reed

gentle.gloss: an easy, singing tone with the buzz held back

full.gloss: the ordinary playing weight, reed clearly audible

hard.gloss: pushed -- the reed's full harmonic series, brash

forced.gloss: the bellows crushed down, the reed at its harshest

rattle.note: the reed's own mechanical noise: a `dust` puff per half cycle through a 2600 Hz resonance, rising and falling with the bellows so it is part of the note and not a separate hiss. The widest of the three axes -- centroid 585 -> 2435 Hz, comb 96.7 -> 35.5 dB, loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

clean.gloss: a pure reed tone, no mechanism audible

breathy.gloss: the slot audible under the note

rattly.gloss: the tongue clearly buzzing in its slot

wheezing.gloss: an old bellows -- as much air and clatter as tone

techniques.code:
kpress  = 0.45                              ; press: how hard the bellows lean on the reed
kmus    = 0.55                              ; musette: one reed, or three spread apart
krat    = 0.30                              ; rattle: the reed's own mechanical buzz
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 24   ; harmonics the band can hold
; The bellows are the instrument's gesture and they never hold still. This cycle
; has to drive the movement, because the musette beat cannot: at kmus=0 there is
; only one reed and nothing to beat against, and the note would then stand.
kbcy    poscil 0.5, 0.19                    ; the bellows lean and ease over ~5 s
kmul    = 0.40 + 0.38 * kpress + 0.09 * kbcy ; pressure opens the series
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kbel    = 0.0011 * kbcy                     ; the same lean pulls the reed slightly sharp
ar1     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kbel), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
ar2     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm * kmus, kf0 * 1.0122, knh, 1, kmul, giCos   ; +21 cents
ar3     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm * kmus, kf0 * 0.9908, knh, 1, kmul, giCos   ; -16 cents
knmus   = 1 / sqrt(1 + 2 * kmus * kmus)     ; detuned reeds are incoherent: power adds
abuz    dust 1.0, kf0 * 2                   ; one puff per half cycle of the reed
anz     rand 0.6, 0.71, 1
arat    reson abuz * 0.35 + anz * 0.12, 2600, 1600, 2
asig    = (ar1 + ar2 + ar3) * knmus * 2.05 \
          + arat * krat * 0.30 * (0.55 + 0.90 * (0.5 + kbcy))

techniques.why: harmonica / blues harp -- a free reed played inside cupped hands, and the hands are the point. The breath drives a `gbuzz` stack; a `reson` cavity that moves with the cupping hand sits FIXED in Hz (380 to 1830, plus a 5.1 Hz hand tremolo), because a cavity is a cavity whatever note is played -- the same reason a vowel's formants do not follow the keyboard. The air hissing past the reed plate rises and brightens with the breath cycle rather than sitting under it as a constant: a steady hiss under a pulsing reed reads as a separate noise generator, and measured, its own variance then swamped every coherent movement in the note (three of eight corners stopped moving). Level held by `balance` against a fixed 400 Hz yardstick: 0.02 dB across the parameter cube, 0.01 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz. Brighter and thinner than `free_reed`; the cavity is what distinguishes them.

cup.note: the hand closed over the shell or opened away from it: a cavity resonance from 380 Hz (closed, dark, muffled) to 1830 Hz (open, bright), with a 5.1 Hz hand tremolo on it throughout. FIXED in Hz, so it colours the same band at every pitch. Centroid 1700 -> 1922 Hz, comb 41.2 -> 37.6 dB, loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

open.gloss: hands away -- the bare reed, bright and direct

cupped.gloss: hands closed -- the hollow, vocal wah of a blues harp

press.note: how hard the breath drives the reed. Deepens the harmonic comb (38.9 -> 42.7 dB) at a nearly constant centroid, which is what a harmonica does when you blow harder -- it gets reedier, not simply brighter. Loudness constant to 0.01 dB.

soft.gloss: a light breath -- sweet and almost whistle-like

overblown.gloss: forced past the reed's comfort -- raw and edgy

breath.note: air past the reed rather than through it. The widest axis: centroid 600 -> 2227 Hz, comb 70.0 -> 31.7 dB. It rises and brightens with the breath cycle, so it moves WITH the note (coherence stays above 0.7 at every corner) instead of adding a static hiss. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

clean.gloss: pure reed, no air audible -- almost an organ

airy.gloss: the breath audible around the note

breathy.gloss: as much air as tone -- intimate, close-miked

gasping.gloss: mostly air, the pitch only just holding through it

techniques.code:
kpress  = 0.50                              ; press: how hard the breath drives the reed
kcup    = 0.40                              ; cup: the hand closed over the shell, or opened away
kbrth   = 0.35                              ; breath: air past the reed rather than through it
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 20   ; harmonics the band can hold
kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.29                    ; the breath opens and closes over ~3.5 s
kb01    = 0.5 + kbr                         ; the same cycle as 0..1
kmul    = 0.44 + 0.34 * kpress + 0.09 * kbr ; breath opens the series
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kwob    poscil 0.0016, 4.7                  ; the breath shakes the reed a few times a second
kslo    poscil 0.0009, 0.127                ; and wanders under that
ahr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kwob + kslo), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
khand   poscil 0.5, 5.1                     ; the hand tremolo: a harmonica's own wah
kcf     = 380 + 1450 * kcup + 300 * khand   ; the cupped hand: a cavity, so FIXED in Hz
acup    reson ahr, kcf, 560, 1
anz     rand 0.5, 0.53, 1
; the hiss IS the breath, so it rises and brightens with it -- a steady hiss under
; a pulsing reed reads as a separate noise generator, and its own variance then
; swamps every coherent movement in the note.
abr     reson anz, 1250 + 750 * kb01, 850, 1
amix    = ahr * (1 - 0.75 * kcup) + acup * 1.20 * kcup \
          + abr * kbrth * 0.40 * (0.35 + 0.95 * kb01)
aref    poscil 0.35, 400                    ; a fixed-loudness yardstick: the hand and the
asig    balance amix, aref, 1               ;   breath must colour, never fade

techniques.why: bagpipe -- a cane reed chanter plus DRONES, which is the whole architecture: a `gbuzz` chanter at pitch, a tenor drone an octave down and a bass drone two octaves down, each detuned from the chanter so all three beat. Measured, the drones take the beat depth from 0.04 to 0.21 and the detune holds that depth while moving the RATE from 1.0 to 4.0 Hz. A piper's bag pressure is steady but not constant, so a 0.13 Hz arm wander opens the series slightly -- without it the note stands perfectly still wherever the drones are turned off, which is how nine of twenty-seven corners failed the movement rule before it was added. Darker than the other reeds here (centroid 571 Hz at 220, against `sax` 1696) because the drones put most of the energy two octaves below the note. Loudness 0.12 dB across the cube, 0.24 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz.

drone.note: the parallel pipes beside the chanter, an octave and two octaves down. Beat depth 0.00 -> 0.21. Centroid 876 -> 500 Hz as the low pipes fill in, comb 102.5 -> 10.7 dB. Power-summed (`knmix`), because detuned pipes are incoherent -- adding them as amplitudes would make this a volume control. Loudness constant to 0.10 dB.

chanter.gloss: the melody pipe alone, no drones -- a solo cane reed

one.gloss: the drones behind the chanter, present but under it

full.gloss: the ordinary balance -- drones as loud as the tune

droning.gloss: the drones dominant, the chanter riding on top

reed.note: how hard the bag pressure drives the cane reed. The brightness axis here, and a wide one: centroid 353 -> 1026 Hz, comb 18.7 -> 13.4 dB (the drones' comb washing out as the chanter fills in). Loudness constant to 0.01 dB.

soft.gloss: an underblown reed -- woody, almost recorder-like

strong.gloss: the reed well up, the characteristic hard edge

screaming.gloss: a highland chanter at full pressure

beat.note: how far out of tune the drones sit. A RATE control, not a depth one: measured, the beat depth stays at ~0.20 while the rate goes 1.0 -> 1.7 -> 2.3 -> 3.3 -> 4.0 Hz. It therefore moves almost no colour at all (centroid 576 -> 577 Hz) and is invisible to every spectral meter; `lco_measure.beat` is what reads it. Loudness 0.10 dB.

tuned.gloss: drones dead on -- a slow 1 Hz swell, nearly still

close.gloss: a gentle 2 Hz beat, the pipes breathing together

loose.gloss: 3 Hz -- audibly untuned, the folk sound

sour.gloss: 4 Hz, the drones fighting the chanter

techniques.code:
kreed   = 0.55                              ; reed: how hard the bag pressure drives it
kdrone  = 0.60                              ; drone: the parallel pipes beside the chanter
kbeat   = 0.45                              ; beat: how far out of tune the drones sit
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 22   ; harmonics the band can hold
; A piper's bag pressure is steady, not constant -- the arm loses and regains it
; slowly, and this small wander is the only movement the chanter has of its own.
; Without it the note stands still wherever the drones are turned off.
kbag    poscil 0.5, 0.13                    ; the arm eases and leans, ~8 s
kmul    = 0.52 + 0.30 * kreed + 0.07 * kbag ; a cane reed under near-constant pressure
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kwob    poscil 0.0010, 6.3                  ; the cane reed chatters
ach     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kwob), knh, 1, kmul, giCos    ; the chanter
knhd    limit int(sr * 0.45 / (kf0 * 0.5)), 1, 22
knrd    = ((1-kmul^knhd)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knhd))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kdt     = 0.004 + 0.014 * kbeat             ; drones are never quite in tune with the chanter
ad1     gbuzz 0.17 * knrd, kf0 * 0.5 * (1 + kdt), knhd, 1, kmul, giCos    ; tenor drone, an octave down
ad2     gbuzz 0.17 * knrd, kf0 * 0.25 * (1 - kdt), knhd, 1, kmul, giCos   ; bass drone, two octaves down
knmix   = 1 / sqrt(1 + 2 * kdrone * kdrone) ; the drones beat against the chanter: power adds
asig    = (ach + (ad1 + ad2) * kdrone) * knmix * 1.95

techniques.why: saxophone -- a single beating reed on a CONICAL bore, and the cone is what separates it from `clarinet`: a cone keeps all harmonics, a cylinder keeps only the odd ones. Measured odd/even balance +4.3 dB here against `clarinet`'s +113 dB, which is the objective signature of the difference. Two `reson` formants at 900 and 1750 Hz, FIXED in Hz, are what make a saxophone shout rather than merely buzz. A 0.68 Hz breath cycle opens the series AND slides the two bore formants with it, so the note moves at every setting: written with fixed formants the colour stood still at every honk above zero, since half the output was then a filter that could not move. The reed hiss rides the same breath rather than sitting under it as a constant -- held at a fixed 0.09 it carried nearly half the measured centroid, and a saxophone tone is not half hiss. Level held by `balance` against a fixed 400 Hz yardstick: 0.00 dB across the parameter cube, 0.00 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz, and 0.01 dB across the two crossed over 162 renders.

honk.note: how much the conical bore shouts: a crossfade onto two narrow `reson` formants at 900 and 1750 Hz. Measured, the centroid falls 1491 -> 1202 Hz monotonically -- the formants concentrate the tone in the middle instead of brightening it. FIXED in Hz, so it colours the same band at every pitch. Loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

veiled.gloss: no bore emphasis -- a plain reed, almost an oboe

round.gloss: the bore just colouring the tone

vocal.gloss: the saxophone's own singing formant, clearly there

shouting.gloss: the full conical honk, midrange forward

blow.note: how hard the reed is driven. It deepens the harmonic comb (39.7 -> 43.1 dB) and more than triples the colour movement in the note (115 -> 373 Hz), at a nearly constant centroid up to three quarters of the way (1341 -> 1417 Hz) -- the two bore formants hold the colour while the series behind them fills in. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

breathy.gloss: barely speaking -- soft, subtone, close to a sine

loud.gloss: pushed, the reed's whole series audible

honking.gloss: blown as hard as the reed takes

growl.note: the player humming against the reed, as amplitude modulation at 74 Hz -- sidebands, not vibrato. Measured, the sideband energy around the harmonics goes 0.0001 -> 0.174 of the carrier energy and the harmonic comb FILLS IN from 48.9 to 26.5 dB as the sidebands crowd between the partials, which is exactly what turns tone into rasp. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

clean.gloss: no growl -- a pure reed tone

edge.gloss: a trace of grit, the tone just roughened

growl.gloss: an audible hummed rasp under the note

roar.gloss: full-throated, the pitch buried in rasp

techniques.code:
kblow   = 0.45                              ; blow: how hard the reed is driven
khonk   = 0.50                              ; honk: how much the conical bore shouts
kgrowl  = 0.15                              ; growl: the hummed note that turns tone to rasp
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 26   ; harmonics the band can hold
kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.68                    ; the breath opens and closes, ~1.5 s a lung
kemb    poscil 1.0, 5.3                     ; the embouchure is never still, and stiffness IS colour
kmul    = 0.42 + 0.30 * kblow + 0.26 * kbr + 0.028 * kemb
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kgr     poscil 1.0, 74.0                    ; the hummed note, a growl not a tremolo
klip    = 0.0012 * kemb                     ; the same motion, two cents of it in pitch
asr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + klip), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
asr     = asr * (1 + 0.60 * kgrowl * kgr)   ; humming AGAINST the reed: sidebands at +-74 Hz
; The bore formant is not a fixed filter: the player's throat and the reed channel
; are part of it, so it slides with the same breath that drives the reed. Without
; this the shout pins the colour in place at every honk above zero.
ahk     reson asr, 900 * (1 + 0.10 * kbr), 260, 1
ahk2    reson asr, 1750 * (1 + 0.17 * kbr), 400, 1
; Reed hiss rises and falls with the breath that makes it -- it is not a fixed
; pedestal. Held at a level it cannot pin the colour with: at 0.09 it carried
; nearly half the measured centroid, and a saxophone tone is not half hiss.
anz     rand 0.5, 0.37, 1
abr     reson anz, 1900, 700, 1
khs     = 0.042 * (0.35 + 1.30 * (0.5 + kbr))
amix    = asr * (1 - 0.80 * khonk) + (ahk * 2.10 + ahk2 * 0.95) * khonk + abr * khs
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: oboe / bassoon / shawm / zurna -- two blades of cane beating against each other, which is the narrowest, most pungent way to make a reed sound. A `gbuzz` stack with an unusually complete harmonic series (comb contrast 70.6 dB against the rest of the reed family's 15-46 dB, though a bare `vco2` waveform reads higher still) through a narrow `reson` cavity whose centre moves 480 Hz (bassoon-deep) to 1580 Hz (oboe-piercing), FIXED in Hz. A 0.23 Hz breath cycle opens the series, which is what makes it move: measured coherence +1.00 at the defaults, and every one of the 27 parameter corners moves. Darker at its default than `sax` (674 vs 1696 Hz) but far more combed -- the pungency is in the completeness of the series, not in the brightness. Level held by `balance` against a fixed 400 Hz yardstick: 0.08 dB across the cube, 0.03 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz.

throat.note: which double reed it is: the bore formant from 480 Hz (bassoon) to 1580 Hz (oboe), plus a weaker one at 2.15x it. FIXED in Hz. Centroid 544 -> 718 Hz, monotone. The formant's absolute prominence FALLS as it rises (the band around it goes 36 % to 2 % of the energy) because a 1580 Hz formant over a 220 Hz note has fewer harmonics to work with -- that is the physics, not a defect. Loudness 0.01 dB.

bassoon.gloss: the deep, hollow, slightly comic low double reed

cor anglais.gloss: between the two -- plaintive and covered

oboe.gloss: the bright, nasal, penetrating orchestral reed

shawm.gloss: the shrillest -- a zurna or suona, outdoors and loud

press.note: how hard the two blades are driven, and the widest axis here: centroid 472 -> 1218 Hz with the colour movement in the note rising from 37 to 172 Hz alongside it. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB through the closed-form `gbuzz` normalisation.

soft.gloss: the blades barely open -- hollow and dark

full.gloss: ordinary playing weight, the reed clearly speaking

pressed.gloss: driven hard -- the piercing double-reed cry

forced.gloss: as much as the blades take, shrill

bite.note: how narrowly the blades pinch the air: the crossfade onto the cavity formants. Measured, the 400-2000 Hz band goes 41 % to 55 % of the energy, monotonically. The centroid dips and returns (717 -> 671 -> 690 Hz) because the formant pulls energy inward from both ends rather than upward -- the band fraction is the honest reading of this axis. Loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

loose.gloss: an open embouchure -- broad and unfocused

pinched.gloss: tight -- the tone concentrated and reedy

biting.gloss: clamped down, all cavity and no body

techniques.code:
kpress  = 0.50                              ; press: how hard the two blades are driven
kthroat = 0.55                              ; throat: bassoon-deep, or oboe-piercing
kbite   = 0.45                              ; bite: how narrowly the blades pinch the air
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 28   ; harmonics the band can hold
kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.23                    ; the breath opens and closes over ~4 s
kmul    = 0.46 + 0.34 * kpress + 0.09 * kbr ; two blades let a lot of the series through
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kwob    poscil 0.0014, 5.9                  ; the blades chatter a few times a second
adr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kwob), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
kcf     = 480 + 1100 * kthroat              ; bore formant, FIXED in Hz: 480 bassoon .. 1580 oboe
afm     reson adr, kcf, 230, 1              ; the reed cavity's shout, narrow
afm2    reson adr, kcf * 2.15, 480, 1       ; the second, weaker one
amix    = adr * (1 - 0.88 * kbite) + (afm * 2.30 + afm2 * 1.10) * kbite
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: mbira / kalimba -- a plucked steel tongue over a resonating board, and the one thing every additive imitation of it gets wrong is the overtone spacing. A uniform clamped-free bar has partials at 1 : 6.267 : 17.55, which is why a `mode` bank built from the textbook ratios sounds like a tuning fork and not like an mbira. A real tine is FORGED THINNER at the struck end, and that taper pulls the overtones down: the second partial sits at 6.27x with no taper, 5.70x at `taper` 0.22 (a commercial kalimba), 5.10x at 0.45 (the measured mbira dzavadzimu, 1 : 5 : 14) and 3.67x when hammered right down. Three `mode` resonators on a continuous `rand` exciter, so a held note stands rather than decaying -- and that standing is what makes movement hard here: at Q 520-900 the bank's centroid wanders 750 Hz on its own, which is a class the movement meter cannot resolve, so a deliberate motion has to stand clear of the wander to count. The player's hand does it, breathing on the board at 0.23 Hz and reaching the TINE and not only the caps -- as a spectral tilt, damping the first mode while freeing the third, plus the brightness of the thumb's own contact noise. Both together, because with only the tilt the interior taper values the 3-step gate never visits still read as standing still. Two things nothing else in the library has: the machachara -- loose bottle caps on the soundboard, a `dust` bed of small metal impacts that is emphatically not a tone -- and the deze, the calabash the whole board sits in. Loudness 0.13 dB across the cube, 0.81 dB crossed with the register, register tilt 0.69 dB.

taper.note: how far the tine is forged down towards its tip, which is the instrument's real timbre control. Centroid 2316 -> 1378 Hz, and the comb contrast is deliberately NOT monotone (25.0, 23.7, 17.0, 24.2, 8.6 dB across the anchors) -- as the partials slide they pass through and away from exact harmonic positions, so the tone alternates between hollow and clangorous. Loudness 0.11 dB.

ideal bar.gloss: a uniform bar -- 6.3x and 17.6x, glassy and remote

kalimba.gloss: a commercial kalimba tine, 5.70x -- a 0.8 tip/root ratio

buzz.note: the machachara: how many caps are on the board and how loose. Centroid 1753 -> 2082 Hz with the comb barely touched (24.2 -> 23.7 dB), which is the signature of adding a non-pitched bed rather than changing the tone. The impact rate rises 320 -> 840 a second alongside. It does not touch the colour movement in the note (2019 Hz at every setting): the hand breathes on the board at 0.23 Hz whatever this is set to, and that breathing reaches the TINE, so no setting can make the instrument stand still. It used to reach only the caps, which this axis scales, so at 0 the movement was multiplied out and what remained was the bank's own noise wander. Loudness 0.00 dB.

clean.gloss: the caps taken off -- bare tines

shells.gloss: a few caps, the usual rattle

swarming.gloss: loose caps everywhere, more buzz than note

gourd.note: the deze the board sits inside, as a Helmholtz cavity at 175-305 Hz. Centroid 1850 -> 1706 Hz and comb 22.7 -> 25.8 dB: a big calabash makes the instrument DARKER and more combed, not louder, because it returns the bottom of the tine's series and nothing above it. Fixed in Hz, so the same box colours every pitch. Loudness 0.07 dB.

board only.gloss: no gourd at all -- thin and papery

big calabash.gloss: a wide 40 cm gourd, deep and boxy

techniques.code:
ktaper  = 0.55                              ; taper: a thick ideal bar, or a forged mbira tine
kbuzz   = 0.35                              ; buzz: the bottle caps rattling on the board
kgourd  = 0.45                              ; gourd: the calabash the whole board sits in
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A real tine is thinner at the struck end, and that taper is what pulls its
; overtones DOWN from the textbook clamped-free bar: 1 : 6.267 : 17.55 ideal,
; 1 : 5.7 : 15.6 at a 0.8 tip/root ratio (kalimba, measured 5.30-5.86),
; 1 : 5.11 : 13.47 at 0.6 -- which lands on the measured mbira dzavadzimu 1 : 5 : 14.
; Those two are tip/root ratios and NOT `taper` values: the code reaches them at
; taper 0.22 and 0.45, which is where the anchors of that name sit.
kr2     = 6.267 - 2.60 * ktaper
kr3     = 17.55 - 9.00 * ktaper
; The player's hand breathes on the board at 0.23 Hz, and it reaches the TINE, not
; only the caps. It used to reach `acap` alone -- which is scaled by `buzz` -- so at
; buzz 0 the movement the note promised "whatever this is set to" was multiplied out,
; and what was left was the mode bank's own noise wander: replacing the LFO with a
; constant changed the measured motion by 0.1 Hz out of 605. A hand pressing the board
; shifts which partials the tines give up, so it is a spectral tilt and not a level:
; the first mode is damped as the third is freed, which `balance` then holds level.
; Two mechanisms, because one was not enough to be SEEN: three `mode` resonators at
; Q 520-900 on a noise exciter wander on their own -- with the hand frozen, 833 Hz of
; centroid span and 1695 Hz of fast motion -- which is the class `moves`
; documents as beyond it, and a deliberate motion has to stand clear of that wander or
; it reads as more of the same. With the tilt alone at a modest depth, taper 0.70 and
; 0.75 -- interior values the 3-step gate never visits -- still measured coherence
; 0.10-0.15. Both together: every taper from 0.0 to 1.0 moves, worst coherence 0.39,
; and the loudness cost is 0.13 dB.
kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.23
arw     rand 0.05, 0.5, 1                   ; a continuous exciter: a held note stands
aex     tone arw, 600 + 5000 * (0.5 + kbr)  ; the thumb's contact brightening and dulling
am1     mode aex * (1 - 0.90 * (0.5 + kbr)), kf0, 900
am2     mode aex * 0.62, kf0 * kr2, 700
am3     mode aex * 0.24 * (1 + 6.00 * (0.5 + kbr)), kf0 * kr3, 520
; the machachara: loose caps on the soundboard, a bed of small metal impacts and
; not a tone, breathing with the same hand
adu     dust 1.0, 320 + 520 * kbuzz
acap    reson adu * 0.30, 3200 + 900 * (0.5 + kbr), 2200, 1
; the deze: a 40 cm calabash is a Helmholtz cavity around 160-340 Hz, FIXED in Hz
kdz     = 175 + 130 * kgourd
adz     reson (am1 + am2), kdz, kdz * 0.55, 1
amix    = (am1 + am2 + am3) * 1.0 + adz * kgourd * 0.85 + acap * kbuzz * 1.90
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

; overtones DOWN from the textbook clamped-free bar: 1 : 6.267 : 17.55 ideal,
; 1 : 5.7 : 15.6 at a 0.8 tip/root ratio (kalimba, measured 5.30-5.86),
; 1 : 5.11 : 13.47 at 0.6 -- which lands on the measured mbira dzavadzimu 1 : 5 : 14.
; Those two are tip/root ratios and NOT `taper` values: the code reaches them at
; taper 0.22 and 0.45, which is where the anchors of that name sit.

; The player's hand breathes on the board at 0.23 Hz, and it reaches the TINE, not
; only the caps. It used to reach `acap` alone -- which is scaled by `buzz` -- so at
; buzz 0 the movement the note promised "whatever this is set to" was multiplied out,
; and what was left was the mode bank's own noise wander: replacing the LFO with a
; constant changed the measured motion by 0.1 Hz out of 605. A hand pressing the board
; shifts which partials the tines give up, so it is a spectral tilt and not a level:
; the first mode is damped as the third is freed, which `balance` then holds level.
; Two mechanisms, because one was not enough to be SEEN: three `mode` resonators at
; Q 520-900 on a noise exciter wander 750 Hz on their own, which is the class `moves`
; documents as beyond it, and a deliberate motion has to stand clear of that wander or
; it reads as more of the same. With the tilt alone at a modest depth, taper 0.70 and
; 0.75 -- interior values the 3-step gate never visits -- still measured coherence
; 0.10-0.15. Both together: every taper from 0.0 to 1.0 moves, worst coherence 0.39,
; and the loudness cost is 0.13 dB.

arw     rand 0.05, 0.5, 1                   ; a continuous exciter: a held note stands
aex     tone arw, 600 + 5000 * (0.5 + kbr)  ; the thumb's contact brightening and dulling

am2     mode aex * 0.62, kf0 * kr2, 700
am3     mode aex * 0.24 * (1 + 6.00 * (0.5 + kbr)), kf0 * kr3, 520
; the machachara: loose caps on the soundboard, a bed of small metal impacts and
; not a tone, breathing with the same hand

acap    reson adu * 0.30, 3200 + 900 * (0.5 + kbr), 2200, 1
; the deze: a 40 cm calabash is a Helmholtz cavity around 160-340 Hz, FIXED in Hz
kdz     = 175 + 130 * kgourd
adz     reson (am1 + am2), kdz, kdz * 0.55, 1
amix    = (am1 + am2 + am3) * 1.0 + adz * kgourd * 0.85 + acap * kbuzz * 1.90

asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: jaw harp / khomus / morsing -- a steel tongue plucked against the teeth, and the clearest case in the library of a source that never changes while the sound changes completely. The tongue gives one dense harmonic comb (68.8 dB contrast) at one pitch; everything the player does is done with the mouth cavity in front of it. That is measurable and is the entry's objective signature: the `vowel` axis moves the centroid 799 -> 1533 Hz while the comb stays constant to 1.0 dB. A filter that shifts the colour and leaves the series untouched is what a resonating mouth IS, and it is why this instrument belongs in a library the author reads for idioms. Loudness 0.03 dB across the cube, 0.12 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.07 dB over five octaves.

vowel.note: the shape of the mouth in front of the tongue, from `oo` to `ee`. Centroid 799 -> 1533 Hz with the comb contrast constant to 1.0 dB and loudness to 0.02 dB. The formants are FIXED in Hz -- a mouth does not transpose with the note -- so the same vowel colours every pitch. The colour movement is LARGEST at the dark closed vowel and smallest at the bright one (399 -> 70 Hz), because the mouth's own travel is a fixed number of hertz: the same swing is a large fraction of an 840 Hz band and a small one of a 2290 Hz band, and down there it also sweeps across a denser part of the series.

ah.gloss: the mouth wide, the classic twang

sweep.note: how far the mouth travels while the note sounds, which is what makes a jaw harp talk. This is the entry's motion axis: the colour movement in the note doubles, 155 -> 307 Hz, at an almost unchanged centroid (1112 -> 1190 Hz) and comb (0.9 dB). It has a floor -- the mouth is never still even at 0, so no setting stops the instrument moving -- and the floor is +-85 Hz rather than +-55 because the movement bound is in CENTS: at the bright vowel 55 Hz of a 2290 Hz band is 58 cents, and three corners measured as standing still while the closed vowel carried the axis. Loudness 0.01 dB.

drifting.gloss: a slow easing of the vowel

wailing.gloss: the mouth swept end to end, a talking wow

pluck.note: how hard the tongue is struck, as the reach of the comb rather than a level. Centroid 1148 -> 1240 Hz and comb 69.4 -> 65.1 dB: harder plucking fills IN the spectrum between the harmonics (the tongue rattles against the frame) instead of adding brightness. Loudness 0.00 dB -- it is not a velocity control; the synth owns that.

snapping.gloss: flicked hard -- the frame buzzing with it

techniques.code:
kvowel  = 0.45                              ; vowel: the mouth from 'ooh' to 'eee'
ksweep  = 0.55                              ; sweep: how far the mouth travels inside one note
kpluck  = 0.30                              ; pluck: the finger against the steel tongue
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; The tine's pitch never changes; what the player plays is which HARMONIC of it the
; mouth picks out. So the source is a dense comb and the melody is a filter.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 42   ; a low harp reaches into the 40s
kmul    = 0.86                              ; a steel tongue through a narrow slit: bright
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
atn     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; The vocal tract's second formant is the one that does the work: measured across
; 76 speakers it runs 840 Hz ('ooh') to 2290 Hz ('eee'). FIXED in Hz -- a mouth is
; a mouth whatever the tine is tuned to, and that is the whole instrument.
; A mouth is never still, so the travel has a floor `sweep` adds to rather than
; being its only source -- at sweep=0 the note would otherwise stand.
; The floor is +-85 Hz and not +-55. At +-55 it was enough at the dark end and not at
; the bright one: `ee` puts the band at 2290 Hz, where 55 Hz is 58 cents and the note
; measured as standing still at three corners. The floor is in Hz and the bound is in
; cents, so the closed vowel was carrying it. The `sweep` axis is untouched by the
; change -- it still moves the colour 155 -> 307 Hz across its range.
kmo     poscil 0.5, 0.41                    ; the mouth walking the band: this is the melody
kf2     = 840 + 1450 * kvowel + (170 + 560 * ksweep) * kmo
kf1     = 270 + 460 * kvowel                ; the first formant follows, lower and weaker
af2     reson atn, kf2, kf2 * 0.11, 1
af1     reson atn, kf1, kf1 * 0.16, 1
; the pluck itself: a steel tongue released by a finger, a few times a second
adu     dust 1.0, 3 + 13 * kpluck
apl     reson adu * 0.22, 1500 + 1700 * (0.5 + kmo), 1500, 1  ; the plucks brighten as the mouth opens
amix    = af2 * 2.30 + af1 * 0.85 + atn * 0.10 + apl * kpluck * 0.40
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1
