techniques.why: didgeridoo / yidaki -- a lip-driven wooden drone, and it is in the library for one specific reason: its harmonics are EXACTLY harmonic even though the bore is a hollowed branch of no particular shape. The lips stay shut for a good part of every cycle, and that periodic closure -- not the bore -- sets the series. So the substrate's `gbuzz` is exactly right and a shaped-bore model would be wrong. What a player actually plays is the vocal tract's IMPEDANCE: where it is high the flow through the lips is choked and the radiated sound has a HOLE. That needs a real band-reject and not a subtracted bandpass -- `butterbr` measures -50 dB at its centre, while subtracting a `reson` moves its own band by 0.2 dB and `areson` is literally that same subtraction, with a shallow dip 200 Hz below where it claims to be. So: one open band with a real choke either side. Because the open band has to carry the tone, what the chain applies is a FORMANT rather than a pair of holes -- measured on white noise through the same chain, -1.7 / +9.2 / -3.3 dB at 1320 / 1650 / 1980 Hz, which is 10.9 and 12.5 dB of peak-to-shoulder contrast. Let the drone through unfiltered instead and the holes go -10.7 and -12.3 dB deep while `tongue` moves 14 Hz of colour: the depth and the axis are one trade, and the formant is the side of it that leaves a control. All three sit FIXED in Hz -- a mouth does not transpose. Humming into the drone is MULTIPLICATIVE, so it makes m*f1 +- n*f2 sidebands rather than a tremolo, and that is what turns the tone to a growl: the comb goes 70.4 dB (a clean harmonic drone) to 14.6 dB (rasp) across `voice`, the widest of this entry's three axes and the third widest in the library -- `pwm`'s rate spans 73.2 dB and `free_reed`'s rattle 60.8, each read against its own fundamental. The open band has to CARRY the tone rather than garnish it -- at a mix that let the unfiltered drone through, the two real chokes cancelled `tongue` to 14 Hz of colour, because moving the whole pattern up moves nothing net while the energy sits below it untouched. Loudness 0.02 dB across the cube, 0.08 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.03 dB.

voice.note: humming a second note into the drone, the way a player growls a didgeridoo. Multiplicative, so it does not sit on top of the tone but multiplies it into sidebands: comb contrast 70.4 -> 14.6 dB and centroid 1068 -> 2523 Hz, the widest of this entry's three by both (and third in the library by comb, behind `pwm`'s rate and `free_reed`'s rattle). The comb is read against the body's OWN fundamental at each anchor, which is not the asked pitch: with the hum full on the sidebands halve it. The hum runs at 97 Hz FIXED, so its sidebands stay where they are while the drone moves with the keyboard -- which is what a voice inside an instrument does, and the beat meter reads that 97 Hz back at a depth of 0.04 -> 0.54. Loudness 0.00 dB.

a hum.gloss: a voice just audible in it

roaring.gloss: hummed hard -- more rasp than note

tongue.note: where the tongue puts the tract resonance, from a closed low vowel to an open high one. The open band's centre sweeps 1150 -> 2150 Hz and the two chokes track it at 0.80 and 1.20 of that. Centroid 1630 -> 1845 Hz -- a much smaller number than the band's own travel, because a formant that moves trades one part of the series for another rather than adding anything, and because the tract only shapes the region above 1 kHz while the drone keeps its weight below. Comb 0.1 dB, loudness 0.02 dB.

open.gloss: the mouth open, the band up

wide open.gloss: the tract wide -- bright and shouting

breath.note: circular breathing, as a pressure pulse and not a level pulse. While the cheeks push, the pressure at the lips falls, so the comb shortens and the tone dulls once or twice a second -- the sound never stops, which is the whole point of the technique. Written as an amplitude pulse this axis moved 8 Hz of colour and 3 Hz of motion, i.e. it was a knob that did nothing while quietly modulating loudness; as a pressure pulse it moves the colour movement in the note 91 -> 481 Hz, a factor of five, at 0.00 dB of loudness and 0.1 dB of comb.

surging.gloss: hard circular breathing, the drone heaving

techniques.code:
ktongue = 0.50                              ; tongue: where the mouth chokes the sound
kvoice  = 0.30                              ; voice: humming into the drone
kbreath = 0.40                              ; breath: the pulse of circular breathing
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; The drone is EXACTLY harmonic even though the bore is not, because the lips stay
; shut for a good part of every cycle. So: a dense harmonic comb, then the mouth.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 30
; Circular breathing does not make the drone louder and softer -- the point of it
; is that the sound never stops. What changes is the PRESSURE at the lips while the
; cheeks push: it falls, so the comb shortens and the tone dulls, once or twice a
; second. Written as a level pulse this was a loudness control that moved 8 Hz of
; colour, which is to say a knob that did nothing.
kbp     poscil 0.5, 1.7
kmul    = 0.80 - 0.17 * kbreath * (0.5 + kbp)
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
adr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; What a player plays is the vocal tract's IMPEDANCE: where it is high, the flow
; through the lips is choked and the radiated sound has a HOLE there. A hole needs a
; real band-reject: `butterbr` measures -50 dB at its centre, where the two ways of
; faking one do not. Subtracting a `reson` -- which is what this body did -- moves its
; own band by 0.2 dB, and `areson` is literally that same subtraction (measured
; identical to the dB), with a shallow -3.5 dB dip that sits 200 Hz BELOW its stated
; centre. Neither notches: the old chain's LOWER trough measured +1.2 dB, a slight
; boost where a hole was called for, while its upper one did notch at -13.0 dB.
; Now one open band with a real choke either side -- and because the open band has to
; carry the tone (see the mix below), what the chain applies is a FORMANT and not a
; pair of holes: measured on white noise through the same chain, -1.7 / +9.2 / -3.3 dB
; at 1320 / 1650 / 1980 Hz, so 10.9 and 12.5 dB of peak-to-shoulder contrast. At a
; mix that let the drone through unfiltered the holes are -10.7 and -12.3 dB deep,
; and `tongue` then moves 14 Hz of colour: the depth and the axis are the same trade.
; The tongue never stops moving, and it has to travel far enough to be heard at the
; TOP of its own axis: at +-210 Hz the band swept 1940-2360 Hz, where a 220 Hz drone
; has barely any energy left, so `breath 0, tongue 1, voice 0` measured 21 Hz of travel
; and stood still. +-350 Hz crosses three harmonics there instead of one.
ktg     poscil 0.5, 0.37
kfc     = 1150 + 1000 * ktongue + 350 * ktg
achk    butterbr adr, kfc * 0.80, kfc * 0.30    ; the flow choked below the open band
achk    butterbr achk, kfc * 1.20, kfc * 0.42   ; and above it
apk     reson adr, kfc, kfc * 0.11, 1           ; the band the tongue opens
; humming against the drone is MULTIPLICATIVE, so it makes m*f1 +- n*f2 sidebands
khm     poscil 1.0, 97.0
; The open band has to CARRY the tone, not garnish it. With the through path at 0.80
; the two real chokes cancelled the `tongue` axis to 14 Hz of colour -- moving the
; whole pattern up moves nothing net while most of the energy sits below it, untouched.
; At 0.40/2.80 the fundamental is still the loudest partial and the band stands +5.4
; and +3.5 dB over its two neighbours, which is what a didgeridoo spectrum looks like.
amix    = (achk * 0.40 + apk * 2.80) * (1 + 0.55 * kvoice * khm)
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: overtone singing / sygyt -- one voice producing a melody out of its own harmonics, and the mechanism is specific enough to be worth an entry: the singer merges the second and third vocal formants into a SINGLE very narrow resonance and tunes it ONTO one harmonic of a dense buzz, so that harmonic alone is let through as a whistle above the drone. Two things are needed for that to be audible and both were missing at first. The window must SNAP to a harmonic -- left sliding it sat between two for most of every cycle and picked neither, measuring 6.8 dB BELOW its own neighbours. And the window must be NARROWER than the harmonic spacing, which at the bottom of the keyboard it was not: at 55 Hz it sat 152 Hz wide across a 55 Hz spacing with three harmonics inside it, and 26 of 162 corners fell under the +7 dB the entry exists for, three of them negative. Bounded by the spacing, the picked harmonic stands +10.4 to +41.4 dB over its neighbours over the whole cube and the whole keyboard, none under +7 -- covering the 15-35 dB measured on Tuvan singers. A lift against the drone's roll-off (a `gbuzz` falls kmul per harmonic, so the 8th to 12th overtone starts 13 to 18 dB under the 2nd) adds 3.9 to 5.1 dB on top of that. It is also where this entry's one open defect is: the lift changes the picked harmonic's LEVEL as the melody steps, so the worst corner of the cube travels 6.66 dB inside a single held note, which §4 does not allow. Every constant tried moves that number rather than removing it (see the code), so it needs a decision about the mechanism. It is also the cleanest example in the library of colour without source change: across `press` the centroid travels 299 Hz while the comb contrast moves only 2.1 dB. Nothing about the voice changes; only which harmonic escapes. Loudness 0.21 dB at its worst axis, 0.34 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.13 dB.

select.note: which harmonic the merged formant sits on, which is the melody the style is for. Centroid 1301 -> 2267 Hz. The window snaps to a harmonic, so this axis picks one and does not land between two: at 220 Hz it walks roughly the 5th to the 11th. Below a fundamental of about 330 Hz the resonance is FIXED in Hz and the drone tracks the keyboard, so which harmonic speaks changes with the note as it does for a singer; above that there is no harmonic left inside a vocal 1.0-2.4 kHz window at all, and it holds at the third rather than collapsing onto the fundamental. Loudness 0.21 dB.

low harmonic.gloss: just above the drone -- barely separate from it

high harmonic.gloss: far up the series -- a thin pure whistle

focus.note: how tightly the two formants are merged, as the Q of the resonance: 9 wide open to 45 at full focus. Almost no centroid change (1688 -> 1844 Hz) and little comb change (3.1 dB), but the colour movement in the note goes 188 -> 310 Hz -- a narrow window makes the same stepping melody audible as a moving whistle, where a wide one averages it away. This is a motion control that looks nearly inert to a colour meter, which is the reason both are reported. Loudness 0.01 dB.

khoomei.gloss: the softer style, harmonic and drone together

sygyt.gloss: the whistling style, harmonic clearly separate

whistling.gloss: as narrow as it goes -- a flute over a drone

press.note: how pressed the voice is, which fills the buzz the formant has to work with. Centroid moves 299 Hz and the colour movement in the note 114 Hz, at 2.1 dB of comb across the whole axis -- a pressed voice has more harmonics for the window to find, not a different spectrum shape. The whistle's own contrast rises gently along it: +10.6, +12.3, +12.9 dB over its neighbours at 110 Hz, and flat within a dB at 220 and 880. Loudness 0.18 dB.

strained.gloss: pushed hard -- rasping, every harmonic there

techniques.code:
kselect = 0.45                              ; select: which overtone the mouth picks out
kfocus  = 0.60                              ; focus: how far the neighbours are pushed down
kpress  = 0.45                              ; press: an open throat, or the pressed drone
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; Sygyt: one drone, and ONE of its overtones standing far above its neighbours.
; Measured on Tuvan singers, the reinforced overtone is the 8th to the 12th and the
; two either side of it are 15-35 dB down, the next pair 35-65 dB. The mechanism is
; linear filtering: the second and third formants MERGE into one very narrow peak.
; No subharmonics -- that is what separates sygyt from kargyraa.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 24
kmul    = 0.62 + 0.30 * kpress              ; a pressed drone carries more overtones
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kjt     poscil 0.0009, 5.3                  ; a voice is never perfectly steady
adrone  gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kjt), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; The merged formant sits FIXED in Hz, between 1.0 and 2.4 kHz, so WHICH overtone
; it picks depends on the note -- exactly as it does for a singer.
; A singer TUNES the merged formant ONTO a harmonic -- that is how one overtone comes
; to stand out instead of the window falling between two -- and walks it in HARMONIC
; steps, which is why sygyt melodies are stepped and not glides. So the window snaps.
; Left sliding continuously it sat between harmonics for most of every cycle and picked
; neither: measured with the melody frozen, the aimed-at harmonic stood 6.8 dB BELOW its
; own neighbours at select 0. Snapped, and with the window narrower than the harmonic
; spacing, it stands +10.4 to +41.4 dB above them over all 162 corners of the cube and
; the keyboard, none under +7 -- which covers the 15-35 dB the note above cites.
;
; The FLOOR is the awkward case, and it is honest about a physical impossibility: above
; a fundamental of about 330 Hz there is no harmonic left inside a vocal 1.0-2.4 kHz
; window at all -- an overtone singer's f0 is 70-400 Hz, and the keyboard goes far
; past that. Pinned at the 2nd, 27 of 27 corners stood still at 1760 Hz and 9 of 27 at
; 880. Held at the 3rd instead, the window has room to walk at every register and
; nothing is static. Below 330 Hz the floor never bites and the formant is fixed in Hz
; as a real tract is; above it, it tracks the note, because there is nothing else there.
; 0.55 Hz and not 0.31 -- and the reason is musical, not measured, which is worth saying
; because it was once the other way round. On an earlier body 0.31 Hz read as wander;
; on this one both rates move and by almost the same amount (travel 220 vs 215 Hz,
; coherence 0.874 vs 0.888), so the measurement no longer decides it. 0.55 stays
; because a sygyt melody is quicker than one step per three seconds. +-0.9 harmonics,
; so it always steps.
kmv     poscil 0.5, 0.55
kna     = (1000 + 1400 * kselect) / kf0     ; the harmonic the vowel aims at
kn      limit round(max(kna, 3) + 1.8 * kmv), 2, knh
kfm     = kf0 * kn
; `limit`ed away from zero: at kfocus 1.2366 the bracket crosses zero and `reson` gets
; a zero bandwidth, which is NaN out. The host cannot send more than 1, but this body
; is read as an idiom and copied.
; A window WIDER than the harmonic spacing cannot pick one harmonic out of the
; series, whatever its gain -- and at the bottom of the keyboard it was: at 55 Hz
; the window sits at the 24th harmonic, so 0.115 * kfm is 152 Hz against a 55 Hz
; spacing, and three harmonics stood inside it. Measured, 26 of 162 corners fell
; under the +7 dB this entry is FOR and three were negative -- no whistle at all.
; Bounded by the spacing: 0 of 162, and the worst corner is +10.1 dB. (The MEASUREMENT
; had to be fixed first: searching harmonics 3..knh for the best contrast excludes the
; top of the series, which is exactly where the window sits at 55 Hz, so a genuine
; +19 dB whistle at the 24th read as -0.5 dB. Search to Nyquist instead.)
kbw     limit kfm * (0.115 - 0.093 * kfocus), kfm * 0.020, min(kfm * 0.200, kf0 * 0.90)
; A `gbuzz` drone falls kmul per harmonic, so the 8th to 12th overtone -- the ones sygyt
; is ABOUT -- start 13 to 18 dB below the 2nd. A narrow formant in a real tract has high
; gain; this is that gain, cancelling the roll-off at whichever harmonic the window
; sits on. What it is NOT is the difference between audible and inaudible: with the
; window bounded by the spacing the whistle already stands +12.1 to +22.2 dB over its
; neighbours with no lift at all, and the lift adds 3.9 to 5.1 dB of that -- measured
; across `select` at 220 Hz. What it also does is move the level as the melody steps,
; which is the open problem recorded at the ceiling below.
; The ceiling is where a held note PUMPS, and it is left at 12 because nothing else
; measured better. Each step of the melody moves the picked harmonic's level
; wherever the lift cannot follow the roll-off, and `balance`'s 1 Hz tracker chases
; the step train instead of removing it: measured over the whole cube and keyboard,
; the worst corner travels 6.66 dB inside one held note, which is loudness moving
; inside a standing tone. Raising the ceiling to 30 takes the corner it was first
; found at (`press` 0, `select` 0.45, 220 Hz) from 6.08 dB to 1.03 -- and moves the
; worst case rather than removing it: 6.75 dB elsewhere, 6 corners of 162 over 5 dB
; against 5 before. Removing the lift outright is worse still (8.47 dB, and one
; corner's whistle drops to +6.9 dB); bounding `kn` to where the lift reaches is
; worse again (11.67 dB). The lift is what turns the step into a level change --
; with it off the level holds to 0.67 dB at that corner -- so this needs a decision
; about the mechanism and not another constant. Recorded in LCO_PARAM_AUDIT.md.
klift   limit kmul ^ (1 - kn), 1, 12
am1     reson adrone, kfm, kbw, 1
am2     reson am1, kfm, kbw, 1              ; twice, for the skirts the merge gives
af1     reson adrone, 520, 190, 1           ; the first formant, left where it is
amix    = am2 * 3.10 * klift + am1 * 0.75 + af1 * 0.55 + adrone * 0.08
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: cicada -- and the reason it is worth an entry is that a cicada has no voice at all. Each rib of the tymbal plate BUCKLES, each buckling is one impulse, and the RATE of the train is what is heard as pitch: measured 100-200 bucklings a second, perceived between 329 and 660 Hz. So the source is a pulse train -- a harmonic series -- and not an oscillator, and because a buckling is a click the series is nearly FLAT rather than rolling off. That is not a detail: built with a mid `kmul` the series was 26 dB down by 5 kHz and the sac axis inverted, making the sound darker as the resonance rose, because the higher band had less to pass. In front of the train sits the abdominal air sac, a Helmholtz resonator measured 3.0-5.3 kHz with the song near 4.3 kHz, FIXED in Hz -- so a cicada an octave up is not a bigger cicada but a brighter one. Loudness 0.01 dB across the parameter cube, 0.02 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.01 dB over five octaves.

ribs.note: how many ribs reach their buckling load, as the flatness of the pulse train. The widest axis here: centroid 1627 -> 3163 Hz and the colour movement in the note 210 -> 1348 Hz, at 0.00 dB of loudness. The comb barely moves (57.5 -> 51.2 dB) because a flatter train is still a train -- what changes is how far up the series reaches, not whether it is one.

few.gloss: only the first ribs go -- a soft tick

all.gloss: every rib buckling -- a shrieking wall of insect

sac.note: where the abdominal air sac resonates, 3000 to 5300 Hz, which is the measured range for real species. Centroid 2038 -> 2614 Hz with the comb untouched at 0.8 dB -- the signature of a resonator in front of an unchanged source. Fixed in Hz, so it colours every pitch the same way. Loudness 0.00 dB.

deep body.gloss: a large abdomen, 3 kHz -- rounder and further off

song.gloss: the measured song band near 4.3 kHz

small.gloss: a small insect at 5.3 kHz -- piercing

rasp.note: how irregular the buckling is, as jitter on the train's rate. Measured as a comb change and not as a colour one: 69.9 -> 44.6 dB of contrast while the centroid moves 611 Hz, i.e. the series smears into a band instead of moving. A real tymbal is not a metronome, and at 0 this reads as an implausibly clean electronic buzz. Loudness 0.00 dB.

insect.gloss: the ordinary unevenness of a real one

tearing.gloss: so irregular the pitch dissolves into noise

techniques.code:
ksac    = 0.50                              ; sac: the abdominal air sac's resonance
kribs   = 0.55                              ; ribs: how many tymbal ribs buckle at once
krasp   = 0.40                              ; rasp: how irregular the buckling is
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A cicada has no voice. Each rib of the tymbal plate BUCKLES, and each buckling is
; one impulse; the ribs go in a train, and the train's RATE is what is heard as pitch
; (measured 100-200 a second, perceived between 329 and 660 Hz). So the source here is
; a pulse train -- which is to say a harmonic series -- and not an oscillator.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 40
; the song swells and eases, and a swelling cicada gets BRIGHTER as well as louder --
; more ribs reach their buckling load. Gating the whole signal would change the level
; and nothing else, since a spectral centroid does not care about scale.
ksw     poscil 0.5, 0.41
; A rib buckling is a CLICK, so the train's series is nearly flat -- not the smooth
; rolloff a mid `kmul` gives. Built at 0.52 the series was 26 dB down by 5 kHz and the
; sac axis fought it: moving the resonance 3000 -> 5300 Hz made the sound DARKER,
; because the higher band had 26 dB less to pass and `balance` then let the tone
; dominate. A flat source is both physically right and what lets the sac speak.
kmul    = 0.80 + 0.13 * kribs + 0.05 * ksw
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kjit    rand 0.006, 0.53, 1                 ; the buckling is not metronomic
atr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + krasp * kjit), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; The abdominal air sac is a Helmholtz resonator, measured 3.0-5.3 kHz with the song
; frequency near 4.3 kHz. FIXED in Hz -- an insect's body does not transpose, which is
; why a cicada an octave up is not a bigger cicada but a brighter one.
kfs     = 3000 + 2300 * ksac
abd     reson atr, kfs * (1 + 0.14 * ksw), kfs * 0.30, 2
amix    = atr * 0.32 + abd * (1.10 + 0.80 * (0.5 + ksw))
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: cricket -- a scraper dragged along a file of teeth, and the tooth-strike RATE is the carrier. That is why the tone is famously almost a pure sine: the file's tooth spacing is tuned to the wing's own resonance (measured 4-5 kHz for a field cricket), so the two coincide by evolution instead of by filtering. The entry rests on a second fact that a distant recording hides: close to, a cricket is NOT one tone -- the scraper dragging over the teeth is audible as broadband noise well above the carrier. That matters mechanically as well as musically, because a pure tone has nothing to move: without the file this body stood still at 18 Hz of travel, and movement by default is not satisfiable by a sine. The file also has a FLOOR, since a cricket always drags it, so no setting can stop the sound moving. Loudness 0.01 dB across the parameter cube, 0.06 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.04 dB over five octaves.

scrape.note: how much of the file is heard against the wing tone. The widest axis here and the one the instrument moves on: centroid 1820 -> 2188 Hz, comb 33.8 -> 24.8 dB and the colour movement in the note 32 -> 221 Hz, at 0.01 dB of loudness. Its share follows the wing speed, so it breathes with the chorus drift at 0.31 Hz whatever this is set to.

clean.gloss: heard from far off -- almost only the tone

close.gloss: a few metres away, the file audible

grinding.gloss: more file than tone -- a dry mechanical scrape

chirp.note: wing closures a second, 12 to 50 -- a RATE, and no spectral meter can see one. Measured on the colour meters this axis moves 2 Hz of centroid and 0.5 dB of comb, which reads as inert and is not: on the beat meter it reads back 12.0, 21.7, 31.0, 40.3 and 50.0 Hz against the 12, 22, 31, 40 and 50 asked, at a pulse depth of 0.34 to 0.41. Dolbear's law is the reason it is a control at all -- an insect's rate tracks temperature -- though Dolbear counted chirp GROUPS per minute, where this is the pulse rate inside them. Loudness 0.01 dB.

cold.gloss: 12 a second -- slow, a cold night

hot.gloss: 50 a second -- almost a continuous tone

pure.note: how sine-like the wing tone rings, as the reach of its harmonic series. Centroid 1980 -> 2087 Hz and comb 31.1 -> 27.7 dB -- a small axis by design, because a cricket's tone is nearly pure at every setting and this only decides how nearly. It deliberately does NOT touch the file: when it did, two axes multiplied and seven corners of the cube stood perfectly still. Loudness 0.01 dB.

reedy.gloss: several harmonics -- a coarser, buzzier insect

whistle.gloss: as pure as the wing goes

techniques.code:
kscrape = 0.40                              ; scrape: how much of the file is heard
kchirp  = 0.50                              ; chirp: wing closures a second
kpure   = 0.60                              ; pure: how sine-like the wing tone rings
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A cricket rubs a scraper along a file of teeth, and the TOOTH RATE is the carrier --
; which is why the tone is nearly a pure sine: the file's tooth spacing is tuned to the
; wing's own resonance, so the two coincide by evolution rather than by filtering.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 10
; A chorus drifts in and out of step, and that slow waver is the only rate the colour
; CAN move at: the wing closures run 12-50 a second, well above what a centroid
; sampled 32 times a second resolves, so a per-pulse colour change is invisible.
kdr     poscil 0.5, 0.31
kmul    = 0.46 - 0.38 * kpure
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
ato     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; Dolbear's law: the chirp rate tracks temperature, about 2.4 Hz at 13 C rising to 5.6
; at 27 C for the snowy tree cricket. A wing closure is one pulse.
kwc     = 12 + 38 * kchirp                  ; wing closures a second
kpl     poscil 0.5, kwc
akg     interp 0.42 + 0.58 * (0.5 + kpl)
; Close to, a cricket is not one tone: the scraper dragging over the teeth is audible
; as broadband noise well above the carrier, and how much of it there is follows the
; wing speed. This is where the colour moves -- a pure tone has nothing to move, so
; without the file the instrument stands still (measured: 18 Hz of travel).
anz     rand 0.6, 0.61, 1
kfs     = kf0 * 5.5
asc     reson anz, kfs, kfs * 0.8, 1
; a floor, because a cricket ALWAYS drags its file: with none of it the instrument
; stood perfectly still (0.6 Hz of travel), and no axis may be able to stop the sound
; moving
; `pure` deliberately does NOT touch this. It did, and then two axes multiplied: at
; scrape 0 with pure 1 everything that moves shrank to nothing and seven corners stood
; still. A pure-toned cricket still drags its file; what `pure` shapes is the TONE.
kscl    = (0.34 + 0.66 * kscrape) * (0.30 + 1.40 * (0.5 + kdr))
amix    = ato * akg + asc * akg * kscl * 0.55
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

The larynx makes a rough buzz and the call is chopped into pulses at 15 to 100 a second, and that rate is what another frog listens for; carriers for pulsed calls run 300 Hz to 2 kHz. So the two axes that carry the instrument are a rate and a depth, and both are invisible to a colour meter -- `pulse` moves 5 Hz of centroid and 50.8 dB of comb contrast, which is the objective signature of chopping rather than filtering. In front of the larynx sits the inflated vocal sac, a resonator FIXED in Hz at 380-1530. Loudness 0.01 dB across the parameter cube, 0.03 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.02 dB over five octaves.

pulse.note: pulses a second, 15 to 100 -- the species marker. On the beat meter it reads back 15.0, 57.7 and 100.0 Hz against the 15, 58 and 100 asked. On the colour meters it moves 5 Hz of centroid and 50.8 dB of comb, because chopping a series at an audio rate puts sidebands around every harmonic and fills the gaps between them -- that comb collapse IS the measurement of the pulsing, not a side effect of it. Loudness 0.01 dB.

slow.gloss: 15 a second -- a deep, countable croak

buzz.gloss: the pulses running into each other

rattle.gloss: 100 a second -- a hard dry rattle, barely pitched

sac.note: how inflated the vocal sac is, as a resonator from 380 to 1530 Hz. The only colour axis here: centroid 358 -> 551 Hz and the colour movement in the note 68 -> 150 Hz at 0.00 dB of loudness. Fixed in Hz, so a big sac is a big sac at every pitch. It also sags and refills at 0.37 Hz, which is where the instrument's movement comes from at every setting.

bullfrog.gloss: a big taut sac -- hollow and booming

croak.note: how deeply the pulses cut into the call, from a smooth buzz to a hard chop. Comb 70.4 -> 55.2 dB at 2 Hz of centroid -- like `pulse` it is a comb measurement and not a colour one, and reading it by centroid alone would call it inert. Loudness 0.01 dB.

clacking.gloss: chopped to near silence between pulses

techniques.code:
ksac    = 0.45                              ; sac: how inflated the vocal sac is
kpulse  = 0.50                              ; pulse: pulses a second in the call
kcroak  = 0.55                              ; croak: how deeply the pulses cut
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A frog codes its species in the PULSE RATE, not in the pitch: the larynx makes a
; rough buzz and the call is chopped into pulses at 15-100 a second, which is what
; another frog listens to. The inflated vocal sac is a resonator in front of it.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 24
; the sac empties as the call runs and refills between calls; a fuller sac drives the
; larynx harder, so this is a colour motion and not only a level one
ksg     poscil 0.5, 0.37
kmul    = 0.60 + 0.16 * ksg
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
alx     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
kpr     = 15 + 85 * kpulse                  ; pulses a second
kpu     poscil 0.5, kpr
kgt     = 1 - kcroak * (0.30 + 0.55 * (0.5 + kpu))
akg     interp kgt * (1 + 0.09 * ksg)
; the vocal sac, FIXED in Hz. A big sac is a Helmholtz resonator low down; a small
; one sits above it. Measured carriers for pulsed calls run 300 Hz to 2 kHz.
kfs     = 380 + 1150 * ksac
asc     reson alx * akg, kfs * (1 + 0.11 * ksg), kfs * 0.42, 1
amix    = alx * akg * 0.30 + asc * 1.35
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

motions.why: dark to bright, ONCE: the spectrum opens over the note and stays open. A one-way gesture — it never travels back. Stands on its own (a filter opening) and is also the opening half of the larger movements.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kpos    = min(knote / 2.5, 1)           ; one-way ramp, holds at the top
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: the timbre keeps travelling and NEVER comes back to where it was. Not a cycle and not a rate: random steps at two speeds, so no state recurs for the length of any note. It must be moving within the first seconds — a note is short.

                                        ; must not move in lockstep
kfj     randi  2.6, 11.0, ivoice        ; the rate itself never settles -- that is flutter
kmot    oscili 0.5, 6.5 + kfj, giSine, ivph
kpos    = kmot + 0.5
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: a regular tremor in the PITCH, about a sixth of a semitone wide -- vibrato. Not a colour movement and not a loudness one: the tone itself wavers, evenly, the way a played note does.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
kv      oscili 0.3, 5.5, giSine, ivph   ; a regular 5.5 Hz tremor, +-0.3 ms of delay
asig    vdelay asig, 2 + kv, 10         ; a modulated delay IS a pitch tremor

motions.why: a regular pulsation of the LOUDNESS, about 4.5 times a second. This is the one movement that touches level rather than colour, because that is what the word means -- but it PULSES and never fades: the note's own envelope still belongs to the player.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
ktr     oscili 0.18, 4.5, giSine, ivph  ; +-1.4 dB, a steady pulse -- never a fade
asig    = asig * (1 + ktr)

motions.why: a glinting in the TOP of the spectrum: the high partials catch the light and let it go again, irregularly. Only the top moves -- the body of the tone stands still. This form re-weights partials that are ALREADY there, so it needs a tone with a bright tail; on a mellow FM tone there is nothing above the highpass to glint with.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
ahi     butterhp asig, 2200             ; the top of the spectrum, on its own
abri    = asig + ahi * 1.2              ; a fixed GLINTING copy of the tone ...
abri    balance abri, asig, 1           ; ... matched to the clean level ONCE
kg      randi  0.5, 9.0, ivoice         ; irregular glints, never a steady beat
kpos    = 0.5 + kg
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + abri * kpos   ; so this can only move COLOUR

alt.when: the tone is FM -- then glint the INDEX, which MAKES and unmakes sidebands instead of re-weighting ones that may not exist
alt.code:
kg      randi  0.45, 9.0, ivoice        ; irregular glints, never a steady beat
asig    foscili 0.5, kfreq * koct1, 1, 2, 3.0 + kg * 3.0, giSine
                                        ; the index itself glints: the
                                        ; sidebands come and go. foscili
                                        ; holds its own level, so nothing
                                        ; has to hold it afterwards.

motions.why: the movement dies away: it stirs at the start and comes to rest, and does not start again. A gesture that decelerates into stillness.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kmot    oscili 0.5, 0.5, giSine, ivph
kpos    = 0.5 + kmot * exp(-knote * 0.35)  ; the movement decays to rest and stays
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: not a movement of its own: it STRETCHES whatever movement is present — halve its rate, or double the time it takes to traverse.
not a movement of its own: it COMPRESSES whatever movement is present — multiply its rate by 1.7, or divide its traversal time by 1.7.
not a movement of its own: it sharply compresses whatever movement is present — triple its rate, or take a third of its traversal time.
